data.title: Mosaic: Efficient CPU-GPU Coordinated Block-Sparse Attention
data.description: arXiv:2605.07719v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long-context LLM serving increasingly relies on CPU-resident context KV cache, driven by KV offloading and disaggregated prefill--decode execution. Although block-sparse attention reduces KV access, existing designs remain inefficient: GPU-centralized execution fetches selected KV blocks from CPU memory at each decoding step, making it PCIe-bound, while CPU--GPU partitioned execution places CPU-side sparse attention on the critical path, leaving substantial GPU time idle. This paper presents Mosaic, a CPU--GPU coordinated block-sparse attention system for efficient long-context decoding with CPU-resident context KV. Mosaic builds on three key insights: output-contribution-aware KV budgeting, head-specific and granularity-aware sparse configuration, and cross-device coordinated scheduling for sparse tasks over CPU-resident KV. Guided by these insights, Mosaic integrates a lightweight head-property predictor, a granularity--budget selector, and a priority-based scheduler to automatically configure and coordinate sparse attention, preserving output quality while improving efficiency on heterogeneous architectures. Across 2 models, 3 benchmarks, and 40 tasks, Mosaic preserves near-FULL quality while achieving a better overall quality--efficiency tradeoff than the evaluated baselines. Compared with the best-quality fixed Quest configuration, Mosaic improves TPOT by up to 3.7$\times$. We further validate Mosaic across four hardware configurations and in a large-model multi-GPU deployment.
data.author: Feiyu Yao, Zhixiong Niu, Xiaqing Li, Yongqiang Xiong, Juan Fang, Qian Wang
